summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's admitted affair with a suspected Chinese spy -- and the board investigation it triggered -- is the biggest story by far today. Apple's push to make Siri more agentic and Goldman Sachs pulling Claude Code from bankers round out AI. Phone picks lean on genuine hands-on content: iPhone Duo cases, a OnePlus 15 ColorOS 17 test, and a fresh deals roundup. 7/10 picks are phone (70%).

topics.working_title: Nvidia's Board Is Investigating Jensen Huang After He Admits an Affair With a Suspected Chinese Spy
topics.why_now: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted in a staff email to a romantic relationship with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, who US intelligence says was recruited by China's top spy agency to collect intelligence on him. Nvidia's board launched an independent investigation within hours. Covered by Nvidia's own statement, Axios, Bloomberg, The Verge, and TechCrunch -- five-plus outlets in under an hour.
topics.angle: Lay out exactly what Nvidia's board statement says, what Huang admitted to in his own words, and what's actually being investigated (vs. what's still allegation).
headline_options: Nvidia's Board Is Investigating Jensen Huang After He Admits an Affair With a Suspected Chinese Spy
Jensen Huang Admits Affair With Alleged Chinese Spy as Nvidia Launches Investigation

sources.title: Nvidia is investigating Jensen Huang's relationship with a Chinese spy -- The Verge

topics.notes_for_writer: Fast-moving story -- stick strictly to what Nvidia's board statement and Huang's own email say; attribute the spy-recruitment claim to US intelligence/NYT reporting, not as settled fact. Nvidia says it has no reason to believe company secrets were compromised -- include that.
